FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A79
Courtesy, cooperation and identifying other users help drivers share the road safely. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A79
A person becomes a pedestrian after leaving a vehicle and must follow pedestrian traffic rules. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A79
Pedestrians should use a sidewalk when available; without one, walk along the left side facing approaching traffic. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A79
At night, pedestrians should improve visibility with a flashlight, light-colored clothing and reflective material. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A79
A pedestrian facing WALK or green should still confirm that drivers see the pedestrian and stop before crossing. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A79
Do not begin crossing against DON'T WALK, red or yellow; if flashing DON'T WALK begins during the crossing, finish crossing. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A79
Pedestrians should make eye contact with slowing or stopped drivers rather than assume they will yield. [A79]
Source: [A79 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A80
Stop for a pedestrian crossing outside a crosswalk even when that crossing is unlawful. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A80
Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, including unmarked crossings where sidewalks meet a street at an intersection. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A80
Yield at a marked midblock crossing just as at a corner crossing. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A80
Stop completely for a crossing pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A80
A green light does not remove the duty to yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A80
Before a left turn or U-turn, search for pedestrians even with a green arrow. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A80
For a right turn, particularly on red, watch pedestrians approaching from the vehicle's right. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A80
Before passing a stopped vehicle, slow and confirm that no pedestrian is crossing ahead of it, including on multilane roads. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A80
Check for pedestrians before backing, especially in busy pedestrian areas such as shopping centers. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A80
Near schools, playgrounds and homes, expect children to emerge between parked vehicles; slow and prepare to stop. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A80
Obey the reduced school-zone speed when lights flash or children are present, and stop for a school patrol's signal. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A80
On the roadway, cyclists have the rights and responsibilities of vehicle users and must follow traffic rules. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A80
Be ready for unexpected bicycle movement because riders differ in skill and may be difficult to see. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A80
Cyclists should ride on the road's right side and obey traffic signs and signals. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A80
Cyclists use hand signals to communicate their intended movement. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A80
A cyclist may use the whole lane when debris, cracks, parked vehicles or another hazard obstructs the riding path. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A80
A cyclist may use the middle or left roadway position for traveling straight through an intersection or making a left turn. [A80]
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A81
The handbook permits cyclists to ride two abreast in a lane, while recognizing situations where single-file riding is preferable. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A81
Cyclists should wear bright clothing and reflectors and keep the bicycle in good repair. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A81
A bicycle headlight is required at dusk; the handbook strongly recommends a taillight for added visibility. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A81
Yield to a cyclist where a bicycle path or lane crosses a road. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A81
Do not stop, park or drive in a designated bike path or lane except to enter or leave an alley or driveway, perform official duties, follow police direction or address an emergency. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A81
When approaching or passing a cyclist, slow, leave generous space and consider the rider's speed. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A81
Do not pass a cyclist immediately before turning right; slow and let the rider clear the intersection first. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A81
After passing a cyclist, avoid an abrupt slowdown or stop that could cause a rear-end collision. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A81
Do not sound the horn close to a cyclist unless a collision risk requires it; a startled rider may swerve. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A81
When turning, watch for cyclists entering the lane, especially children riding from a sidewalk. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A81
Do not turn sharply across a cyclist's path or force the cyclist off the road. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A81
Although cyclists should follow traffic direction, drivers should search for them anywhere on the roadway. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A81
Wet pavement, sand and gravel impair bicycle braking and turning, requiring additional caution nearby. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A81
A cyclist may need both hands for control and be unable to signal; watch head movements and shoulder checks for other intent clues. [A81]
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A82
Before opening a parked vehicle's door, check beside and behind for cyclists and other traffic. [A82]
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A82
The handbook's Dutch Reach example uses the right hand on the door handle to turn the body toward approaching rear traffic. [A82]
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A82
Check for cyclists before backing, with extra attention near schools and residential areas. [A82]
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A82
A sharrow combines a bicycle image with two chevrons and recommends a bicycle's position within a shared lane. [A82]
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A82
A bike lane designates roadway space for bicycles, commonly near the right edge and marked with a solid white boundary. [A82]
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A82
A bike lane does not prevent a cyclist leaving it to avoid a collision, continue straight through an intersection or make a left turn. [A82]
Source: [A82 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0082]

Misconceptions: A cyclist or motorcyclist may need a full lane; another rider's signal does not prove a turn; a truck's leftward setup can precede a right turn; transit and school-bus rules differ.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: identify the user, protect the gap, confirm the path. It adds no road-user entitlement or legal exception.
Glossary: Distinguish sharrow, bike lane, bike route, No-Zone, move-over response, pedestrian safety zone and slow-moving triangle using the source-bound blocks.
Dynamic facts: Edition-bound legal definitions and distances require issuer refresh. Undated statistics, red-signal procedure, sign-image geometry and contradictory instructions remain typed debt; no current-law clearance is implied.

FACT_ID: sec09-F45 | anchor: A83
Bike routes or bikeways recommend lower-traffic roads, often neighborhood or side roads, for bicycle travel. [A83]
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F46 | anchor: A83
Motorcycle, scooter and moped riders have the same traffic rights and responsibilities as other drivers. [A83]
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F47 | anchor: A83
Motorcycles, scooters and mopeds may use a full lane, and two such vehicles may share a lane. [A83]
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F48 | anchor: A83
Do not pass a motorcycle, scooter or moped within the same lane. [A83]
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F49 | anchor: A83
Check mirrors and turn the head to search blind spots for small motorized riders before lane moves and at intersections. [A83]
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F50 | anchor: A83
The handbook defines a motorized bicycle or moped as a two-tandem-wheel or three-wheel device powered by a person, helper motor or both, with all four features: at most3.5 brake horsepower, at most130cc, automatic transmission and a design-speed maximum of30 mph. [A83]
Source: [A83 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F51 | anchor: A84
Do not assume a motorcycle, scooter or moped will turn merely because its signal flashes; wait until the turn begins. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F52 | anchor: A84
Signals on small motorized vehicles may not self-cancel, and some such vehicles may lack signals, so leave maneuvering space. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F53 | anchor: A84
Signal before merging or changing lanes so riders can anticipate the movement. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F54 | anchor: A84
Expect riders to change speed or position around potholes, gravel, slick surfaces, pavement seams, tracks or grooves. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F55 | anchor: A84
When following a motorcycle, scooter or moped, allow three to four seconds, with more space in wet conditions. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F56 | anchor: A84
Dim high beams when approaching a motorcycle, scooter or moped to avoid dazzling the rider. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F57 | anchor: A84
When a rider passes, maintain lane position and speed without accelerating or interfering with the pass. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F58 | anchor: A84
Scooters and mopeds generally travel more slowly than motorcycles. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F59 | anchor: A84
During an emergency, emergency-vehicle drivers may have traffic-control exemptions but must still consider other road users' safety. [A84]
Source: [A84 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0084]
